body.statement: For the family \(\mathcal W_n\), if \(h_n\le1/32\), every honest connected interval in the definition of \(L_n\) satisfies \[L_n(\kappa_n)\ge2a_\star\left[1-2\alpha-\sqrt{\frac{\left(1+\frac{256}{315}\kappa_n^2h_n\right)^n-1}{J_n}}\right]_+.\] In particular, if \(T_n=o(\log(1/\kappa_n))\), then \(\liminf_nL_n(\kappa_n)\ge2a_\star(1-2\alpha)\), including sequences for which \(L_n^{\mathrm{known}}(\kappa_n)\to0\).
body.justification: The bound exhibits a nonshrinking causal interval-length cost created solely by translated unknown cutoffs.
body.gap: MullerSong1997 and Tuvaandorj2020 derive cutoff-location rates for directly observed jumps; neither converts location multiplicity into fixed-level connected LATE-interval length under a vanishing denominator.
body.consumer: Empirical fuzzy-RD analyses with administratively undocumented cutoffs can use the theorem to diagnose when reporting a short connected LATE interval is impossible.
body.proof_tex:
Let \(I_n\) be any interval rule satisfying the honesty condition in def:minimax-length.  Every component of \(Q_{+,n}\) belongs to \(\mathcal P_n\) and has effect label \(a_\star\), whereas every component of \(Q_{-,n}\) belongs to \(\mathcal P_n\) and has label \(-a_\star\), by prop:outcome-invariant-witness.  Averaging the componentwise coverage inequalities gives
\[
 Q_{+,n}\{a_\star\in I_n\}\ge1-\alpha,\qquad
 Q_{-,n}\{-a_\star\in I_n\}\ge1-\alpha.
\]
For probability measures \(Q\ll R\), Cauchy--Schwarz gives
\[
 \operatorname{TV}(Q,R)
 =\frac12E_R\left|\frac{dQ}{dR}-1\right|
 \le\frac12\sqrt{\chi^2(Q,R)}.
\]
The triangle inequality for total variation and the equal chi-square formulas for the two labels therefore imply
\[
 \operatorname{TV}(Q_{+,n},Q_{-,n})
 \le\sqrt{\frac{\left(1+\frac{256}{315}\kappa_n^2h_n\right)^n-1}{J_n}}.
\]
Transferring the second coverage event from \(Q_{-,n}\) to \(Q_{+,n}\), and then using the union bound under \(Q_{+,n}\), yields
\[
 Q_{+,n}\{-a_\star,a_\star\in I_n\}
 \ge1-2\alpha-
 \sqrt{\frac{\left(1+\frac{256}{315}\kappa_n^2h_n\right)^n-1}{J_n}}.
\]
The left side is nonnegative.  A connected subset of \([-1,1]\) containing both labels has length at least \(2a_\star\).  Consequently
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal P_n}E_P[|I_n|]
 \ge E_{Q_{+,n}}[|I_n|]
 \ge2a_\star\left[1-2\alpha-
 \sqrt{\frac{\left(1+\frac{256}{315}\kappa_n^2h_n\right)^n-1}{J_n}}\right]_+.
\]
Taking the infimum over honest rules proves the finite-sample inequality.

It remains to verify the stated limit.  The condition \(T_n=o(\log(1/\kappa_n))\) forces \(\kappa_n\to0\), since otherwise \(T_n=n\kappa_n^{2+1/s}\) diverges at least linearly along a subsequence while \(\log(1/\kappa_n)\) stays bounded.  Thus \(h_n\to0\), and eventually \(h_n\le1/32\).  For such \(n\), since \((16h_n)^{-1}\ge2\),
\[
 J_n\ge\frac1{32h_n}.
\]
Using \(1+x\le e^x\), the chi-square term is bounded by
\[
 \frac{\exp\{(256/315)n\kappa_n^2h_n\}}{J_n}
 \le32h_n\exp\left\{\frac{256}{315}
        \left(\frac{32}{M}\right)^{1/s}T_n\right\}.
\]
Its logarithm is at most
\[
 O(1)-\frac1s\log(1/\kappa_n)
 +\frac{256}{315}\left(\frac{32}{M}\right)^{1/s}T_n,
\]
which tends to \(-\infty\) by the assumed little-oh relation.  The square-root term consequently tends to zero, proving
\[
 \liminf_nL_n(\kappa_n)\ge2a_\star(1-2\alpha).
\]
Finally, the assertion about shrinking oracle intervals is nonvacuous.  For any \(0<\gamma<(2+1/s)^{-1}\), take
\[
 \kappa_n=\rho_n(\log n)^\gamma
\]
for all sufficiently large \(n\).  Then \(\rho_n/\kappa_n=(\log n)^{-\gamma}\to0\), so thm:known-cutoff-benchmark gives \(L_n^{\mathrm{known}}(\kappa_n)\to0\), while
\[
 T_n=(\log n)^{\gamma(2+1/s)}=o(\log(1/\kappa_n)).
\]
This proves the final clause.
